table.method: Dataset and benchmark of 11 recommenders: price-based, collaborative (LightGCN, MF, kNN, association rules), popularity, hybrid LambdaMART.
table.data: 29,090 customers, 388,049 transactions (2018-2022); 61 cutoffs, 6-month window; nDCG@10 and ROI@10. Best nDCG@10 LightGCN 0.3404; popularity 0.2710.
table.limit: Ranks only never-bought assets and drops test repurchases, so no recency baseline exists; no LLM. My question keeps repurchases (61% of purchases in my pilot).

table.method: Qwen3 (0.6-8B) tuned with KTO; prompt holds the customer's transaction graph and a market graph; the model generates 3 ISINs.
table.data: FAR-Trans; test cutoffs Dec 2021 - Jun 2022, 180-day window; Pref@3, Prof@3, Comb@3; best Pref@3 0.5341 (1.7B).
table.limit: Hits@3, not nDCG@10; no candidate pool, no recency baseline, repeat and new purchases not separated. Nearest prior work.

table.method: Six sequential recommenders analysed separately for repeat-next and explore-next users.
table.data: Diginetica, Yoochoose; leave-one-out; Recall, MRR, NDCG.
table.limit: Repeat-next users are a minority but carry most of the average accuracy; authors advise reporting both groups. E-commerce, no LLM.

table.method: Zero-shot LLM ranker (ChatGPT) with sequential, recency-focused and in-context prompts.
table.data: MovieLens-1M, Amazon Games; leave-one-out; NDCG over 20 candidates or candidates from several generators.
table.limit: LLMs struggle to perceive the order of the history and show position and popularity bias. No repurchases, no finance.

table.method: Off-the-shelf LLMs score repurchase candidates; compared with a frequency heuristic and supervised XGBoost.
table.data: Instacart, Dunnhumby, proprietary retail; 100-user samples; NDCG@10.
table.limit: “LLM scores are not competitive with supervised rankers”: the risk my ranker faces on past assets; groceries, closed models.

nearest: FLARKO [9] is the closest study: it tunes small open-weight Qwen3 models on FAR-Trans and shows that LLM-generated top-3 lists match later purchases (Pref@3 up to 0.5341 on a 180-day window), with 1.7–4B models often best; RAG-FLARKO [10] adds knowledge-graph retrieval. It leaves open how an LLM compares with a recency rule when repurchases count, whether its hits are known or new assets, and how a retriever–ranker split behaves; LlamaRec [11] shows that in such a split the ranker can only improve cases the retriever already found.
gap: I did not find a study reporting nDCG@10 of an LLM-based recommender on FAR-Trans under a protocol that keeps repurchases, nor one on financial transactions that separates an LLM encoder’s retrieval of never-bought assets from an LLM ranker’s ordering of the customer’s own past assets against a recency baseline and same-information classical controls.
